title: Refuse `git checkout -B` or `git switch -C` of any branch a worktree holds
why: Coordinator 14:34 CST: `git checkout -B <current branch>` in an agent worktree left a stale index twice.
note: A guard change, so a build lane (test-author, builder, reviewer). Done check: a red test on `git checkout -B <current branch>` in an agent worktree. Nov 7 22:47 CST: lane roadmap-push-refusal-says-fetch (#1777) hit it twice more: an agent's `git checkout -B` left old files in the worktree and index. Possible false alarm in the same incident: the shared-trees guard refused restoring stale staged files that match origin's blobs in an agent worktree; unchecked. Scope widened (coordinator, 03:16 CST Nov 8): one rule refusing `checkout -B` or `switch -C` of any branch a worktree holds. Folded in: checkout-b-held-branch (git 2.43 lets `checkout -B <b>` / `switch -C <b>` reset a branch ANOTHER worktree has checked out, leaving that worktree's index stale; seen 02:49 CST Nov 8 in lane idle-lane-steps-unknown). Lane moved: session_013NEJL1N3YkCMouc1pELXyu ended 02:48 CST with its work on archive/checkout-b-current-branch; lane idle-lane-steps-unknown (session_013NEJL1VtpMs3Aw5JLtyvVD) takes it. Round 2 of #1889 measured that a plain own-worktree `checkout -B lane-x other` is harmless on git 2.43.0, so #1889 narrows to sibling holders only (coordinator ruling, 04:50 CST Nov 8). Triage asked lane roadmap-push-refusal-says-fetch (session_013NEJL4KjioFCNuafMd8V8Q) for the Nov 7 22:47 CST conditions; if they reproduce, the own-worktree refusal comes back, red first.
